Chargeback Handling Procedure
Document Version: 1.0 | Effective Date: 20 August 2026
1. Purpose
This procedure explains how to respond when a customer disputes a completed transaction through their card issuer (a chargeback), as distinct from a direct refund request made to us.
2. When a Chargeback Applies
The customer disputes a charge directly with their bank rather than contacting support first.
The dispute is filed after a transaction has already completed and settled.
The customer claims the service was not delivered, or does not recognize the charge.
3. Handling Steps
Verify: Confirm the transaction exists and check delivery/usage records.
Gather Evidence: Collect delivery confirmation, login/usage logs, and prior support correspondence.
Respond: Submit evidence to the card network within the issuer deadline, typically 7-14 days.
Record: Log the chargeback outcome and evidence packet on the case file.
4. Related Pattern
Chargebacks filed on services the customer continued using after the dispute was raised should be treated as a possible friendly-fraud pattern and cross-checked against usage logs before evidence is submitted.

Customer Communication Templates
Effective Date: 20 August 2026
1. Initial Acknowledgement
Thank you for reporting this to us. We have opened an investigation into the
activity you flagged and will keep you updated as we review it. In the
meantime, no further action is needed from you.
2. Requesting Additional Evidence
To continue investigating your case, could you please provide any of the
following: a screenshot of the transaction, any related emails or messages,
and the approximate time the activity occurred.
3. Resolution Notification
Your case has been resolved. Based on our review, the affected funds have
been restored to your account. Please allow 3-5 business days for the
balance to reflect. Thank you for your patience.
4. Usage Note
Adjust the tone and specifics to match the case; these are starting points,
not scripts to be used word for word.

Device and Browser Verification Guide (Internal)
Document Version: 1.0 | Effective Date: 20 August 2026 | Access: Manager
1. Purpose
Internal reference for evaluating device fingerprint and browser session signals during account takeover review. Distribution is limited to management to avoid publicizing the exact detection thresholds used.
2. Signals Reviewed
Device ID mismatch against the account's known device history.
Browser or user-agent change within the same session.
IP geolocation inconsistent with the account's recent activity.
Session token reuse across two different device fingerprints.
3. Escalation Thresholds
One new signal: log only, no action required.
Two new signals within the same session: require step-up verification (OTP).
Three or more new signals combined with a high-value action: auto-hold and escalate to Account Security.
4. Handling Note
These thresholds are intentionally not shared with front-line staff scripts or customer-facing material, since detailed knowledge of the exact trigger counts could be used to stay under them.

Fraud Escalation Contact Matrix (Internal)
Effective Date: 20 August 2026 | Access: Manager
Severity: Low
Handled by: Assigned case owner. SLA: 3 business days. Escalate to: N/A.
Severity: Medium
Handled by: Department lead (see recommended department on the case).
SLA: 1 business day. Escalate to: Fraud Operations Manager.
Severity: High
Handled by: Fraud Operations Manager. SLA: 4 hours.
Escalate to: Head of Risk, then Compliance if funds cannot be recovered.
Note
This contact matrix is for internal routing only and should not be shared
in customer-facing communication.

Fraud Handling Procedure
Document Version: 1.0 | Effective Date: 17 August 2026
1. Purpose
This procedure provides a simple workflow for identifying, reviewing, documenting, and resolving potentially fraudulent transactions.
2. Fraud Indicators
Multiple transactions using unusual payment patterns.
Repeated failed payment attempts followed by a successful transaction.
Unexpected changes to customer or payment information.
Transactions that do not match the customer's normal activity.
3. Handling Steps
Detect: Flag the transaction using system alerts or manual review.
Review: Check transaction details, account history, timestamps, and supporting evidence.
Restrict: If necessary, temporarily hold the transaction while the investigation is ongoing.
Escalate: Send suspicious or high-risk cases to the responsible fraud/risk team.
Resolve: Approve, reject, refund, or release the transaction based on the investigation.
Record: Document the decision, evidence reviewed, and action taken.
4. Example Case
Transaction TXN-20260817-003 was flagged after several failed payment attempts followed by a successful payment from a new device. The transaction should be reviewed, supporting evidence collected, and escalated if the activity cannot be verified.
5. Important Note
Staff should avoid making assumptions based only on a single indicator. A transaction should be assessed using the available evidence and the organization's fraud controls.

Refund Policy
Effective Date: 17 August 2026
1. Overview
This policy explains how customers may request refunds for eligible transactions. Refund requests are reviewed
based on the transaction status, payment method, and reason provided.
2. Eligible Refunds
A refund may be considered when a transaction was duplicated, incorrectly charged, cancelled before
fulfillment, or affected by a verified system/payment error.
3. Non-Eligible Refunds
Refunds may be rejected for completed services, unauthorized requests without supporting information, or
requests submitted outside the applicable refund period.
4. Processing Time
Approved refunds are normally processed within 5–10 business days. The time required for the funds to appear
may depend on the customer's bank or payment provider.
5. Refund Request Information
Required Information	Example
Transaction ID	TXN-20260817-001
Customer Name	John Tan
Reason	Duplicate payment
Supporting Evidence	Payment receipt / screenshot
6. Contact
Customers should contact the support team with the transaction ID and relevant evidence when submitting a
refund request.
